why: Min-p 0.1 cuts every token below a tenth of the top token, which at the base's diffuse forks removes the spread-out progress alternatives and leaves the easy cyclic step (risk aversion), so loops return and offset the few wrong branches it removes: slightly below the 410 at plain T 1.0.
At T 1.5 more alternatives clear the min-p bar, so loops fall, but the base's forks are diffuse and heating samples more wrong branches there, so accuracy drops well below 410.

Top-p 0.95 at T 1.0 trims the diffuse tail at forks, which cools them a little and brings back some cyclic-step cap hits, so a small loss against the 410 at top-p 1.0 (as top-p 0.95 cost 24 at T 0.6).
RL's forks are near one-hot after entropy collapse, so min-p truncation changes almost no sampled token and RL stays at its 463.
Min-p's relative threshold deletes the diffuse progress mass while the cyclic token stays above it, so rule-A loops reappear at T 1.0 (0 without min-p), though fewer than the 71 at T 0.6.
The loops from min-p add to the 27 non-loop cap hits of plain T 1.0 sampling.
